transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Tara Nguyen (Redwood AE), Marco Silva (Redwood SE), Leah Romero (CTO - NovaHealth), Sanjay Patel (Head of IT), Iris Chen (Cloud Engineer), Nate Brooks (Security)

Auto-generated Summary: (may be imperfect) Discussed private VPC deployment, VPC peering options, region restrictions, KMS integration and SOC2 requirements.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Tara Nguyen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm tara from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. with me is marco, our solutions eng. how's everybdy doing?
[00:08] Leah Romero: good thanks, a bit on the long day but excited to get into this.
[00:12] Marco Silva: hey folks. quick agenda, we want to understand your current infra, data residency needs, security requirements, and map out a proof of concept if that makes sense.
[00:23] Sanjay Patel: sounds good. high level, we run most of our workloads in us-east-1 and us-west-2, some sensitive data must stay in us-east-1 only. region residency is a big one for us.
[00:35] Tara Nguyen: understood. are you primarily looking at Redwood private / private control plane, or exploring dedicated first?
[00:42] Leah Romero: we're evaluating private control plane behind our VPC. Dedicated is interesting too but the control plane separation and audit logs are key. also want private endpoints so nothing traverses public internet.
[00:54] Marco Silva: great — our Private offering supports a customer-managed VPC with a private control plane. we can do VPC peering or transit gateway, and private endpoints for the inference nodes and control plane; we also integrate with customer KMS in most major clouds.
[01:10] Nate Brooks: couple of quick q's re encryption — we need HSM-backed keys or at least customer-managed KMS. do you support external HSMs or bring-your-own-key?
[01:19] Marco Silva: yes, we support BYOK to most KMS providers, and we have HSM integrations for enterprise customers. small note, the first pass may use KMS with customer-managed keys, HSM add-on sometimes requires additional legal/data flow review.
[01:33] Iris Chen: network wise, how does peering work? do you expect us to create routes and security groups? can you go over NAT?
[01:40] Marco Silva: you will create the peering connection from your VPC to the Redwood managed VPC, accept it, and add route table entries. for egress, we support private egress with NAT inside your infra or we can route through a customer-managed NAT gateway. sometimes customers want all outbound traffic blocked and only allow specific flows to Redwood endpoints.
[01:58] Sanjay Patel: what's the IP range requirement on your side? we need to avoid overlaps with our existing ranges.
[02:03] Tara Nguyen: good question — typical ask is a /20 block per environment, but we can work with different sizes. we'll need your CIDR ranges to validate no overlap.
[02:12] Leah Romero: region constraint again — can you guarantee nodes only spin up in us-east-1 for our account?
[02:18] Marco Silva: yes, you can pin region. with Private, you choose the deployment region and we can restrict routing so inference never leaves that region. if you want multi-region redundancy we can set up cross-region peering but that has compliance implications.
[02:32] Nate Brooks: audit logs — we need audit logs to go to our SIEM and have retention for 3 years. is that supported?
[02:39] Marco Silva: audit logs can be delivered to your S3 or object store or pushed via our log forwarder. retention and export policies are configurable; for 3 years we'd typically set up lifecycle policies on the storage side. we'll share the specifics.
[02:51] Sanjay Patel: any limitations on model types in private? like large context models or quantized variants?
[02:57] Marco Silva: most open models we support; we do recommend variants that are validated on the runtime. some bleeding-edge quantization paths require kernel support on certain GPUs. we'll map model catalog to your workload during the PoC.
[03:12] Tara Nguyen: can i ask about traffic patterns — is this synchronous request/response for UI use, or batch scoring?
[03:18] Leah Romero: mostly synchronous interactive with a couple high-throughput batch jobs. latency is important for product-facing flows.
[03:25] Marco Silva: okay that's helpful — for low-latency we can provision dedicated pools, or use auto-bursting. there is a tradeoff: smaller pools + aggressive autoscale can be more cost efficient but may add cold-start latency.
[03:42] Iris Chen: what about private endpoints for embeddings store? we want our embeddings to stay in our VPC and not be stored on a third-party bucket.
[03:49] Marco Silva: embeddings can be stored in your object store or we can provide a private s3-compatible endpoint. the recommended approach is to keep embeddings in your own storage and point Redwood at it via private networking.
[04:02] Sanjay Patel: curious about SSO — we use SAML 2.0 Okta, and want RBAC enforced.
[04:08] Tara Nguyen: SSO via SAML is supported, and RBAC roles can be mapped to your identity provider. for Private we offer enterprise connectors and SCIM provisioning.
[04:18] Leah Romero: security review will want network diagram and data flow. can you send that after the call?
[04:25] Tara Nguyen: yes i'll send the network diagram and a VPC peering checklist. we'll also attach SOC2 and ISO docs.
[04:31] Nate Brooks: one more — any mandatory egress to third-party services? like telemetry to your control plane?
[04:36] Marco Silva: minimal telemetry for health checks — control plane talk can be proxied over a private link; we can also give you an option to disable non-essential telemetry. we'll document which ports and FQDNs are required.
[04:49] Sanjay Patel: do you support Transit Gateway? we use AWS TGW for most cross-account peering.
[04:55] Marco Silva: yes transit gateway is supported; many enterprise customers use TGW for scaling peering across multiple accounts. we can provide a TGW attachment workflow.
[05:06] Leah Romero: pricing — rough numbers for a 3-month PoC with dedicated pool?
[05:12] Tara Nguyen: i can pull some ballpark numbers now but will send formal estimate. very rough: depends on GPU class and number of concurrent workers. i'll include that in the follow-up.
[05:20] Iris Chen: are you able to do network tests or we run perf tests? we'd like to run a benchmark against our network to measure latency to the inference nodes.
[05:27] Marco Silva: we can provide a benchmark harness and sample load generator. for private deployments we can run from within your VPC or from our test harness in the same region. we recommend running from inside your VPC to capture real egress/routing differences.
[05:40] Tara Nguyen: ok let's talk timeline — are you planning to kick off PoC before end of quarter?
[05:45] Leah Romero: hoping to start early january, we'd like to get legal and security sign-off before then.
[05:51] Nate Brooks: legal will need data residency commitments and a DPIA for patient data, plus a BA A? (broken wording, meant BAA).
[05:59] Tara Nguyen: yes we can provide a BAA and DPIA template; will coordinate with legal.
[06:05] Sanjay Patel: network specifics — we'll share CIDR blocks and aws account ids after this call.
[06:10] Iris Chen: on the technical side can you send sample terraform modules or cloudformation templates for the peering?
[06:15] Marco Silva: absolutely, we have infra-as-code samples and a quickstart repo. will include in the follow-up.
[06:22] Leah Romero: ok any known gotchas? like if we want HSM-backed keys and strict egress deny rules is there a long lead time?
[06:30] Marco Silva: HSM integrations can introduce a bit more legal and architecture work, usually a couple weeks to validate. also if you need strict egress deny and private endpoints only, we do some additional testing to ensure nothing falls back to public endpoints.
[06:45] Sanjay Patel: curious about monitoring — can we hook into per-route latency traces?
[06:50] Marco Silva: yes our console has per-route latency and per-token cost breakdowns; for Private we can forward traces to your tracing backend via OTLP.
[06:58] Tara Nguyen: all right let's capture next steps and owners.
[07:02] Leah Romero: sounds good.
[07:05] (brief cross talk about calendars)
[07:18] Tara Nguyen: recap — i'll send network diagram, VPC peering checklist, SOC2/ISO docs, terraform quickstart, and a ballpark PoC cost. marco will prepare a sizing estimate and performance harness. you'll share CIDRs and account IDs. schedule deep dive for 12/9.
[07:36] Nate Brooks: ok thanks.
[07:38] Marco Silva: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs.
[07:40] Meeting end.

Notes: Transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., BAA called out awkwardly). References: sent artifacts to be attached (network-diagram.pdf, soc2-summary.pdf, terraform-quickstart.zip).
